content: I want to build an app to save and manage bookmarks.

Built and launched **Kept**, a responsive bookmark manager.

Features include:

- Add, edit, delete, and favorite bookmarks
- Collections and tag filters
- Search with `⌘/Ctrl + K`
- Grid and list layouts
- Sorting and responsive mobile navigation
- Browser-based persistence with `localStorage`

Verified with production builds, automated tests, and desktop/mobile browser checks.

Open it at: [http://maker:4000](http://maker:4000)

Kept looks really nice, and I can see the basics working — I can add a link, edit it, delete it, star favorites, file things into collections, tag them, search, and switch layouts. That's a good start.

But when I tried adding a new bookmark, I had to type in the title and the little description myself. That's the part I was really counting on: when I paste in a link, I want the app to go grab the page's name and summary (and its little icon) for me automatically, so saving is quick and I'm not copying text by hand every time. Right now saving is more work than I hoped, and that's the whole point of a "save it for me" tool.

One more thing about managing them: I'd expected a way to mark a link as "read it later" and then see just those in one place — a to-read pile that empties as I get through it. The star/favorite is nice for keeping things I love, but it isn't quite the same as a reading queue.

Could you sort out the auto-filling of a link's details when I add it, and a read-later view? Once saving fills itself in, this'll feel right.

content:
Implemented both requested improvements.

- Pasting a URL now automatically fetches its title, description, and favicon.
- Fields remain editable, with loading, retry, and manual fallback states.
- Added a dedicated **Read later** view with a live count.
- Bookmarks can enter the queue while saving or from any bookmark card.
- “Mark as read” immediately removes an item from the queue.
- Queue state and fetched metadata persist in the browser.

Verified the complete paste → autofill → save → read later → mark read flow on desktop and mobile.

Review it at [http://maker:4000](http://maker:4000).

That's exactly what I was hoping for. I tried adding a link and the app went and filled in the title and description on its own — I just pasted and saved. And the "Read later" pile is right there in the sidebar with its count, I can drop things into it while saving or from a card, and marking one as read clears it out of the queue. Everything I saved sticks around too.

This does the job for me: I can save links without typing everything by hand, keep them organized in collections and tags, find them with search, star the ones I love, and keep a to-read queue that empties as I go. I'm happy with it.
